reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Measuring against the slipped vertebra instead of the one below.
name: Meyerding Grading of Spondylolisthesis

version.label: Meyerding (1932), grades I–V
version.detail: Slip of the superior vertebra relative to the inferior, as a percentage of the inferior vertebral body's anteroposterior width. Grade V (spondyloptosis) was added later and is widely used.

purpose: Grades the degree of vertebral slip in spondylolisthesis.
intendedPopulation: Patients with spondylolisthesis on lateral radiograph, CT or MRI.

resultStates.label: Grade I
resultStates.summary: Up to 25% slip of the vertebral body width.

resultStates.label: Grade II
resultStates.summary: 26–50% slip of the vertebral body width.

resultStates.label: Grade III
resultStates.summary: 51–75% slip of the vertebral body width.

resultStates.label: Grade IV
resultStates.summary: 76–100% slip of the vertebral body width.

resultStates.label: Grade V
resultStates.summary: Over 100% (spondyloptosis) of the vertebral body width.

clinicalContext.text: Grades I–II are 'low grade' and III–V 'high grade' in common usage.

clinicalInsights.text: Flexion-extension films show dynamic instability, which the grade does not.

limitations.text: Static measure; does not show instability or slip angle.

limitations: Measurement varies with positioning (supine MRI may under-show slip).

guideSections.what: Five grades of slip by percentage of the inferior vertebral body width.
guideSections.howToPerform: Divide the inferior endplate into quarters; note where the posterior corner of the superior vertebra lies.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with symptoms, dynamic films and slip angle.

sources.citation: Meyerding HW. Spondylolisthesis. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1932;54:371-377.
